title: Iron Infusion in Brisbane: What to Expect, Who Needs It, and How It Works
html:
What Is an Iron Infusion?

An iron infusion is a medical procedure in which iron is delivered directly into the bloodstream through an intravenous (IV) cannula. Unlike oral iron tablets or liquid supplements – which must be absorbed through the gastrointestinal tract – IV iron bypasses the gut entirely, achieving near-complete bioavailability and avoiding the digestive side effects that make oral iron difficult for many patients to tolerate.

At Australian Longevity Clinic in Brisbane, iron infusions are administered under the direct supervision of our registered medical practitioners. All patients require a prior blood test confirming iron deficiency before treatment can be prescribed.

Who Needs an Iron Infusion?

Iron deficiency is one of the most common nutritional deficiencies in Australia, particularly among women of reproductive age, pregnant women, and people with certain medical conditions. An iron infusion may be recommended when:

Oral iron has failed or is not tolerated. Many patients experience significant gastrointestinal side effects from oral iron supplements, including nausea, constipation, stomach cramps, and dark stools. For these patients, IV iron provides an effective alternative.

Iron deficiency is severe. When ferritin levels are very low or haemoglobin is significantly reduced, oral iron may not replenish stores quickly enough. IV iron can restore iron levels within days rather than the months required with oral supplementation.

Absorption is impaired. Conditions such as coeliac disease, inflammatory bowel disease, and gastric bypass surgery can significantly reduce iron absorption from the gut, making IV delivery the most reliable option.

Rapid replenishment is needed. Athletes, women preparing for pregnancy, or patients recovering from surgery may need iron levels restored quickly, making IV infusion the preferred approach.

Diagnosing Iron Deficiency: What Blood Tests Are Required?

Before prescribing an iron infusion, our doctors will review your blood results. The key markers we assess include:

| Blood Test | What It Measures | Normal Range | |---|---|---| | Serum ferritin | Iron storage levels | 30–300 µg/L (women); 30–400 µg/L (men) | | Serum iron | Circulating iron | 10–30 µmol/L | | Transferrin saturation | How much iron is bound to transport protein | 20–50% | | Haemoglobin | Red blood cell oxygen-carrying capacity | 120–160 g/L (women); 130–170 g/L (men) | | Full blood count | Overall blood cell picture | Varies |

A diagnosis of iron deficiency anaemia requires both low ferritin and low haemoglobin. Iron deficiency without anaemia (low ferritin, normal haemoglobin) is also clinically significant and may cause symptoms including fatigue, hair loss, poor concentration, and reduced exercise tolerance.

What to Expect During an Iron Infusion

The iron infusion process at Australian Longevity Clinic is straightforward and well-tolerated by most patients.

Before the infusion: You will have a brief consultation with our doctor to review your blood results, confirm your medical history, and ensure there are no contraindications. You do not need to fast before an iron infusion, and you can drive yourself home afterwards.

During the infusion: A small cannula is inserted into a vein in your arm. The iron solution is delivered slowly over approximately 15 to 60 minutes, depending on the product used and the dose prescribed. You can relax, read, or use your phone during the infusion. Our clinical staff monitor you throughout the procedure.

After the infusion: Most patients feel well immediately after the infusion and can return to normal activities straight away. Some patients notice a temporary metallic taste during the infusion, which resolves quickly. Mild fatigue or a slight headache in the hours following treatment is occasionally reported but is generally short-lived.

How Long Does an Iron Infusion Take?

The infusion itself typically takes between 15 and 60 minutes. The total appointment time, including the pre-infusion consultation and a brief observation period afterwards, is usually 60 to 90 minutes. We ask all patients to remain at the clinic for at least 15 minutes after the infusion is complete as a precaution.

How Quickly Will I Feel Better?

The timeline for iron stores to normalise following an infusion varies between individuals and depends on the severity of deficiency and other clinical factors. A follow-up blood test is recommended 6 to 8 weeks after the infusion to confirm that iron levels have been adequately restored and to determine whether further management is needed.

Are There Any Side Effects or Risks?

Iron infusions are generally safe when administered in a clinical setting by qualified medical professionals. The most commonly reported side effects include:

Injection site reactions – mild bruising, redness, or discomfort at the cannula site, which typically resolves within a day or two.

Temporary discolouration – if any iron solution leaks outside the vein (extravasation), it can cause a brownish discolouration of the skin at the injection site. This is uncommon with modern IV iron products and careful technique, but can be permanent if it occurs. Our clinical team takes every precaution to minimise this risk.

Hypersensitivity reactions – serious allergic reactions to IV iron are rare but possible. This is why all iron infusions at Australian Longevity Clinic are administered in a clinical setting with appropriate emergency protocols in place, and why we observe all patients for at least 15 minutes after the infusion.

Temporary symptoms – some patients experience mild flushing, headache, nausea, or muscle aches during or shortly after the infusion. These are generally transient and resolve without treatment.

How Much Does an Iron Infusion Cost in Brisbane?

The cost of an iron infusion in Brisbane varies depending on the clinic, the iron product used, and whether a Medicare rebate applies. At Australian Longevity Clinic, we will provide you with a clear cost breakdown at your consultation. In some cases, iron infusions may attract a partial Medicare rebate – our team can advise you on this based on your specific circumstances.

Book an Iron Infusion in Brisbane

If you have been diagnosed with iron deficiency or are experiencing symptoms such as persistent fatigue, hair loss, shortness of breath, or poor concentration, an iron infusion may be an appropriate treatment option.

Australian Longevity Clinic is located at 628 Ipswich Road, Annerley, Brisbane – conveniently accessible from the inner south Brisbane suburbs. Complete our online health questionnaire to book your consultation. Please bring your most recent blood test results if you have them, as this will allow us to assess your suitability at the first appointment.
